findings.F1: The book's gain is mostly timing, not the market's own rise: of its mean daily gain of 0.0567 % over 1461 days, 0.0097 % comes from the coins' normal drift and 0.0469 % from timing (t 2.69). The whole gain t is 3.22.
findings.F2: The book earns on the long side only. Long bars sum +8.15 (timing +5.88, 3557 bars). Short bars sum −0.52 (2431 bars). The shorts sit mostly where the close is deep below the 20-day high: the bin more than 3 swings below has a mean position of −0.13 and sums −0.30.
findings.F3: The gain is carried by closes above the 20-day high. Long bars with the close above the high are 754 of 3557 long bars (21 %) and bring +3.43 of the +8.15 long gain (42 %). The three above-high distance bins sum +3.49 on 787 in-profile bars.
findings.F4: On the non-overlapping grid, the drift-removed move after a close above the high is large but rests on few cases:
findings.F5: The plan's 5-day horizon understates the effect; 10 days measures it best:
findings.F6: The above-high excess 10-day move appears in every 60-day trend quartile (+18.1 %, +2.5 %, +26.8 %, +4.7 %) and in both agitation halves (+13.4 % calmer, +10.9 % more agitated). Below the high it stays between −5.2 % and +0.8 %. So it does not live in one agitation profile inside the rising market. The above-high counts are 7 to 20 per cell.

no_ideas: The book earns from long positions after closes at or above the coin's 20-day high in a rising market, best read over about 10 days (F3–F5), and the profile map already holds exactly these ideas as 034-01.e1 (rising market breakout distance continuation) and 034-01.b1 (nearness to high over 10 days), so the findings point to no idea or discovery that the research does not already hold.
